description: Bitemporal legal applicability schedule separating publication time from legal enforceability time across EU (post-Digital Omnibus 2026/1744), US Federal & States, China, UK, South Korea, Japan, Brazil, Singapore, ISO/IEC 42001, IHL, Cyber treaties, and binding CJEU/ICJ judicial precedent.

rules.scope_note: Chapters I and II (AI definitions, AI literacy, and initial eight Article 5 prohibited AI practices).
rules.amendment_notes: Article 4 AI literacy softened in 2026 to focus on practical guidelines rather than mandatory formal certifications; two additional Article 5 prohibitions (non-consensual sexual deepfakes & CSAM) enter application on 2026-12-02.
rules.penalty_ceiling: Up to EUR 35,000,000 or 7% of worldwide annual turnover (Article 99(3))

rules.scope_note: Chapter V (General-Purpose AI Models), Notifying Authorities, Governance, and Penalties (except Art. 101 fines on GPAI providers phased 12 months later).
rules.legacy_note: GPAI models placed on the market before 2025-08-02 have until 2027-08-02 to achieve compliance (Article 111(3)); GPAI fines under Article 101 apply from 2026-08-02.
rules.penalty_ceiling: Up to EUR 15,000,000 or 3% of worldwide annual turnover (Article 101)

rules.scope_note: Article 50 transparency obligations (direct interaction disclosure, synthetic machine-readable watermarking, deepfake labeling).
rules.legacy_note: Legacy generative AI systems placed on the market before 2026-08-02 have a transition window until 2026-12-02 for Article 50(2) machine-readable markings.
rules.penalty_ceiling: Up to EUR 15,000,000 or 3% of worldwide annual turnover (Article 99(4))

rules.scope_note: Standalone High-Risk AI Systems listed in Annex III (biometrics, critical infra, education, employment, essential services/credit, law enforcement, migration, justice) and FRIA (Article 27).
rules.amendment_notes: POSTPONED from original 2026-08-02 deadline to 2027-12-02 by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI). Note: AI Act Article 5 prohibitions and Article 50 transparency STILL apply earlier!
rules.penalty_ceiling: Up to EUR 15,000,000 or 3% of worldwide annual turnover (Article 99(4))

rules.scope_note: High-Risk AI safety components embedded in Annex I Union harmonisation product legislation (medical devices, machinery, aviation, automotive, toys).
rules.amendment_notes: POSTPONED from original 2027-08-02 deadline to 2028-08-02 by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
rules.penalty_ceiling: Up to EUR 15,000,000 or 3% of worldwide annual turnover (Article 99(4))

rules.scope_note: All provisions of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (interpreted by binding CJEU jurisprudence including SCHUFA C-634/21, Schrems II C-311/18, and Meta C-252/21).
rules.penalty_ceiling: Up to EUR 20,000,000 or 4% of worldwide annual turnover (Article 83(5))

rules.scope_note: Mandatory manufacturer reporting of actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents via ENISA Single Reporting Platform (24h early warning / 72h notification).
rules.penalty_ceiling: Up to EUR 15,000,000 or 2.5% of worldwide annual turnover (Article 64)

rules.scope_note: Full Cyber Resilience Act essential cybersecurity, SBOM, conformity assessment, and CE marking requirements for products with digital elements.
rules.penalty_ceiling: Up to EUR 15,000,000 or 2.5% of worldwide annual turnover (Article 64)

rules.scope_note: NIS2 Directive transposition and national supervisory enforcement.
rules.penalty_ceiling: Essential entities: EUR 10,000,000 or 2% turnover; Important entities: EUR 7,000,000 or 1.4% turnover (Article 34)

rules.scope_note: Digital Operational Resilience Act for EU financial entities and Critical ICT Third-Party Service Providers.
rules.penalty_ceiling: CTPP periodic penalty payments up to 1% of average daily worldwide turnover (Article 35(6))

rules.scope_note: UN Convention against Cybercrime (Hanoi Convention, A/RES/79/243). Opened for signature Oct 25, 2025 through Dec 31, 2026; requires 40 ratifications under Article 65 to enter into force.
Biden-era Executive Order 14110 (signed 2023-10-30) was FORMALLY REVOKED on 2025-01-20. NIST AI RMF 1.0 (AI 100-1) and GenAI Profile (AI 600-1) remain active voluntary technical standards.

Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 149 / TRAIGA) enforceable by the Texas Attorney General from Jan 1, 2026; Colorado SB 24-205 revised by SB 26-189; California AB 2013 effective Jan 1, 2026 & SB 53 (TFAIA) frontier disclosures.
rules.penalty_ceiling: Civil penalties enforced exclusively by the Texas Attorney General (60-day cure period for curable violations)

rules.scope_note: China CAC Algorithmic Recommendation (2022), Deep Synthesis (2022), Generative AI Interim Measures (2023), and Mandatory AI-Generated Synthetic Content Labeling Measures + GB 45438-2025 (effective 2025-09-01).
rules.penalty_ceiling: Administrative rectification, service suspension, and statutory fines under PRC Cybersecurity Law & CAC orders

rules.scope_note: South Korea Framework Act on the Development of AI and Creation of a Foundation for Trust (Act No. 20676 & Presidential Decree No. 36053) — Asia's first comprehensive binding statutory AI law.
rules.penalty_ceiling: MSIT corrective orders and administrative fines up to KRW 30 million (initial grace/guidance period for technical compliance)

rules.scope_note: Japan AI Promotion Act (Act No. 53 of 2025) — promulgated 2025-06-04; AI Strategy Headquarters & AI Basic Plan chapters entered full force 2025-09-01.
rules.penalty_ceiling: No direct EU-style administrative fines; mandatory government investigation cooperation and public naming of non-compliant operators

rules.scope_note: UK Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 (2025 c. 18) reforming UK GDPR Article 22 automated decision-making, paired with UK DSIT pro-innovation principles and UK AI Safety Institute (AISI).
rules.penalty_ceiling: ICO enforcement under UK GDPR / Data Protection Act 2018 (up to GBP 17.5M or 4% global turnover)

rules.scope_note: Singapore IMDA Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI (2026) — authoritative voluntary governance standard for tool-calling autonomous AI agents.
Brazil AI Bill PL 2338/2023 approved by Federal Senate (2024-12-10); currently under Chamber of Deputies Special Committee (PL233823) review — NOT YET ENACTED.

ISO/IEC 42001:2023 AI Management System Standard — voluntary internationally certifiable standard referenced as statutory safe harbor / conformity anchor across EU AI Act, Colorado AI Act, and South Korea AI Basic Act.

Geneva Conventions of 1949 (universal ratification; customary IHL) and Additional Protocol I of 1977 (entry into force 1978-12-07; core rules of distinction, proportionality, precautions, and weapons review reflect customary international law).
Geneva Conventions I (Wounded & Sick), II (Shipwrecked), and III (Prisoners of War) of 12 August 1949 — universally ratified binding treaty and customary international law.
Additional Protocol II of 8 June 1977 governing Non-International Armed Conflicts (NIAC).

Binding CJEU preliminary ruling (Case C-634/21, 7 Dec 2023): Automated generation of a probability/credit score strongly relied upon by a third party constitutes a prohibited 'decision based solely on automated processing' under GDPR Article 22(1).

Binding CJEU Grand Chamber ruling (Case C-311/18, 16 July 2020): Invalidated EU-US Privacy Shield and mandated Transfer Impact Assessments + supplementary safeguards for SCC transfers exposed to foreign intelligence surveillance.

Binding CJEU Grand Chamber ruling (Case C-252/21, 4 July 2023): National competition authorities may assess GDPR compliance; personalized AI ad profiling cannot rely on 'contractual necessity' or routine 'legitimate interest' under GDPR Articles 6(1) and 9.

Binding CJEU Grand Chamber ruling (Case C-511/18, 6 Oct 2020): Restricts general and indiscriminate electronic communications retention and automated real-time traffic analysis except for genuine, present, foreseeable national security threats subject to independent judicial review.

ICJ Advisory Opinion (8 July 1996, UN Doc. A/51/218): Affirms that the cardinal principles of distinction and prohibition of unnecessary suffering are 'intransgressible principles of international customary law' and that IHL + the Martens Clause apply to all new weapons technologies.
